title: Sundial Communications on‑prem capacity & Terraform hardening draft
content:
Purpose:
Draft playbook for Sundial Communications' initial on‑prem/private deployment. Focus areas: conservative capacity sizing for p99 latency SLOs, Terraform module hardening (remote state, locking, secrets), network hardening requirements, upgrade & cutover plan, rollback hooks, and testing matrix. This is a working doc — contains TODOs and open questions.

Audience:
Sundial infra architects, Redwood private deploy SREs and solutions eng, platform security reviewer.

Background/context:
Sundial will run customer-facing AI features behind their VPC. Their requirements: 100 rps peak inference (95% text gen, 5% embedding), 8k average prompt length, 99.9% availability SLA internal target, on‑site HSM for key custody, and no internet egress for inference traffic. They requested an on‑prem installation in their colocation (Equinix) with Redwood control plane in a VPC peered over Direct Connect.

Goals & constraints:
- Meet p95 < 120ms, p99 < 450ms for text gen workload at 100 rps.
- Option to enable quantized variants if throughput demand increases.
- Private control plane over peered VPC; only control/control-plane egress allowed via signed endpoints.
- Use their HSM (PKCS#11) for model key material; Redwood to integrate with provided HSM middleware.
- Terraform-only infra automation; minimal manual cutover.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Each GPU node is an A100-80GB equivalent; latency profiles from benchmark run on 2024-11-05 (internal perf repo).
- Average tokens per response = 150 tokens.
- KV cache sticky sessions will be enabled to preserve session-level state; requires consistent client affinity.
- Network RTT between control plane peered VPC and customer colo <= 18ms. If >30ms, fallback plan required.

Initial sizing (conservative):
- Serving tier: 6 inference nodes (GPUs): 3 primary + 3 spare for N+1 at peak. Expected steady throughput ~120 rps with batching heuristics.
- Headroom recommendation: reserve capacity for 2x traffic spikes (reserve 2 extra nodes to enable autoscale up).
- Control plane nodes: 3 small instances (m6a.large-equivalent) in customer VPC for proxying control plane traffic and metrics forwarding (HA pair + arbiter).
- Redis (caching/KV): 3 nodes, 32GB RAM each, persistent disk with RDB snapshots; cross-az replication.
- Storage for artifacts: 2x 2TB NFS mounts (for model store + logs).
- Network: /22 internal allocation for services; designated /28 for management plane endpoints.

Terraform module notes (hardening and patterns):
- Modules to refactor: redwood/vpc-peering, redwood/control-proxies, redwood/serving-cluster, redwood/kv-redis, redwood/hsm-integration.
- Remote state: use S3-compatible object store provided by Sundial (minio) with DynamoDB locking equivalent via Consul TTL. Current PR: linked_artifacts[1]. Ensure state encryption with customer KMS.
- Secrets: do NOT store plain secrets in TF. Integrate TF with HashiCorp Vault on customer infra via consul-template. We propose vault-approle method.
- Providers: pin provider versions in modules and release a compatibility matrix. Lock terraform versions using .terraform-version file.
- CI/CD: add an approval step that runs plan + static checks (tfsec) and posts plan summary to Slack #onprem-deploy-sundial.
- Output artifacts: modules must emit ids for LB, ASG, and route tables to be consumed by deployment pipeline.

Upgrade & cutover plan (4 phases):
1) Preflight (2 weeks): collect final ip ranges, test certificate chain, mock-control-plane handshake in staging colo; run perf microbenchmarks with representative model.
2) Staging deploy (3 days): deploy scaled-down cluster (1 GPU node) with real model weights, end-to-end traffic via synthetic harness.
3) Canary (1 day active): enable 10% real traffic; health checks for 24h. Verify p99 and error budgets.
4) Cutover (weekend 6h maintenance window): scale to production nodes, shift traffic via DNS weight and LB reweight. Keep canary at 10% for 2h then ramp.

Rollback hooks:
- Terraform plan must include a staged apply that creates new resources then migrates traffic. If errors exceed thresholds or tail latency spikes >2x baseline, rollback by reweighting DNS and scaling down new nodes.
- DB snapshot + redis RDB snapshots taken before cutover.

Observability & testing matrix:
- Metrics: per-route latency breakdown, token/sec, kernel occupancy, GPU memory pressure, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio.
- Traces: distributed traces via OTEL collector to customer tracing backend (TLS-only).
- E2E tests: 1) smoke (latency), 2) regression prompts (quality), 3) QPS soak (6h at 1.2x expected load), 4) failover test (simulate GPU node failure).

Network hardening checklist:
- No public ingress to serving nodes; LB must be internal.
- Mutual TLS for control-plane + management endpoints.
- HSM traffic restricted to management subnet; only provisioning host may talk to HSM.
- iptables rules to only allow ports (22 for jump hosts, 443 for control, 8080 for metrics within VPC).

Quantization / model compatibility notes:
- For sequences >4k tokens fallback to float32 model due to attention kernel constraints; add fallback policy in runtime routing.
- Quantized models require additional preflight QA: correctness tests against core eval set.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Customer to confirm HSM vendor and PKCS#11 version (TODO: Sundial to share vendor logs).
- Confirm whether customer wants local model repo mirrored or pull-from-redwood-on-demand. Mirror increases storage and sync complexity.
- Ask security if Vault approle meets Sundial compliance (TODO assigned to Rosa).
- Evaluate if their colo provides a managed Redis (they prefer self-hosted). If managed, adjust TF accordingly.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected network latency -> Mitigation: preflight RTT tests + offline inference mode with local control-plane cache.
- Risk: TF remote state lock not compatible with customer environment -> Mitigation: provide fallback using local state + documented manual locking process.
- Risk: HSM integration delays -> Mitigation: initial deployment using customer-supplied soft HSM (temporary) and scheduled cutover to real HSM.

Acceptance criteria before production signoff:
- Performance: p99 within agreed SLOs for 72h continuous run at 1.0x traffic.
- Security: mutual TLS and HSM connectivity tested; secrets stored in Vault.
- Infra: terraform plans reproducible (CI green) and admin runbook validated.

Owners & timeline (high level):
- Priya (redwood) — infra plan + cutover lead (owner).
- Liam — TF module refactor + PR. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Rosa — security review & HSM integration. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Marcus — SRE: observability + runbooks. ETA: 1.5 weeks.
- Proposed cutover weekend: 2025-03-08 (tentative, pending Sundial calendar).

Next steps (immediate):
- Send this draft to Sundial infra team and schedule a 60m alignment call (owner: Priya).
- Sundial to share HSM vendor details and internal IP ranges.
- Open INF-4821 for tracking tasks (linked).

Notes to self / working reminders:
- Add small script to TF CI that validates no plain-text ARNs in codebase.
- Keep incremental module changes small; tag releases with semantic versions.
- Slack thread: #onprem-deploys -> reference plan and PRs.

End of draft.
